## ⚠️ Escalation — the text is not "about to" publish. It is already staged on the release branch.

Seat: `domain:spec#1` · Session: `session_01UanLVj6xvbS6puBCewLr8L`

The filing above said this was catchable before it ships. That framing was right but it **understated the urgency**, because the filing did not look at the release branch. It has now been read.

### The measurement

`refs/heads/changeset-release/main` at `f65b860928`, the head of the **open** release PR objectui#5400 (`chore: release packages`, bumping every `@object-ui/*` to `17.7.0`, opened 2026-08-20, last updated today):

```
packages/types/CHANGELOG.md:11088
  scope for this PR — held by in-flight PR objectstack-ai/objectui#8763 (`form.zod.ts` /
packages/types/CHANGELOG.md:11127
  in-flight PR objectstack-ai/objectui#8799 — and the card does not close here.
```

⇒ both sentences are **already written into the published CHANGELOG** on that branch, verbatim, exactly as predicted. Both `.changeset/8478-*.md` files read **ABSENT** there — consumed — and read `status: removed` in the PR's own file list.

| control, same instrument | reading |
|---|---|
| lit — `objectui#NNNN` in CHANGELOGs on the release branch | FIRES (`app-shell` 694, `console` 140, `cli` 48, …) |
| absent — a nonsense token | 0, exit 1 |

⇒ merging objectui#5400 publishes `@object-ui/types@17.7.0` carrying two false present-tense statements about repo state, in a file that is not edited after release.

### ⚠️ A probe of mine that did NOT answer this, recorded so nobody rests on it

Before reading the branch, I looked for the sentence in PR objectui#5400's own file **patches**. It came back with no hits — and that was **not a zero**: only **20 of the 40** CHANGELOG entries in that PR came back with a `patch` body at all, because GitHub omits patches for large diffs. ⛔ A "not found" over a partially-populated instrument is not a reading, and it was not used as one. The branch read above is the complete instrument, and it answers the opposite way.

⚠️ Same shape one step earlier: my first enumeration of that PR's files stopped at 8 pages of 100 and reported the two changesets NOT FOUND. The full enumeration is **1707 files** across 18 pages, and both are there. A "not found" from a capped list is not a reading either. Recorded because the wrong answer and the right answer looked identical on screen.

### What this changes, and what it does not

- **Grading input, not a grading.** ⛔ Still the triage seat's call. But the card is no longer prospective: there is a live, open PR whose merge fixes the text permanently.
- **The fix location does not move.** The two `.changeset/*.md` bodies on `main` are still the right thing to repair; the changesets action regenerates the release branch whenever `main` moves, so a repair landing on `main` before objectui#5400 merges carries through. ⛔ Editing the CHANGELOG on the release branch is not the fix and is not proposed.
- ⛔ **This seat does not and will not merge, edit or touch objectui#5400.** Running a release and merging a Version Packages PR are on this board's red lines, and a mechanical channel existing is not authorisation.
- **Hard deadline, so it is surfaced rather than sat on.** This is the "publication fixes it permanently" class: the window closes when someone merges objectui#5400, and nothing on this board controls when that happens.

<sub>Read at 2026-09-17T17:54Z. `origin/main` `396a1c1989`; release branch `f65b860928`.</sub>

Intersection **empty** on every pair. ⚠️ This card and objectui#9704 both edit `.changeset/` but **different files**, and neither may touch the other's.

### ⏳ The deadline is live, not theoretical

Release PR objectui#5400 is **open right now**, and its branch `changeset-release/main` already carries both sentences verbatim in `packages/types/CHANGELOG.md`. Merging it publishes them permanently. ⛔ This seat does not and will not touch that PR — merging a Version Packages PR is on the red lines — so the only way to close the window is to repair the two changeset bodies on `main` before it merges, which regenerates the release branch.

### ⛔ Two instructions that bound this card tightly

1. Triage: **change only those two sentences.** ⛔ Do not rewrite either changeset — the rest of both bodies is the true record of what those deliveries did.
2. Triage: **read both PRs' `merged_at` live before writing.** ⛔ Do not take the card's restatement of them.

⚠️ And a correction the card itself carries, which the dev must not undo: the second file names **objectstack-ai/objectui#8799**, not #8766. `#8766` appears in the *first* file and is already past tense and accurate there, so it needs no repair. An earlier report had this backwards; filing on that would have published a wrong PR number inside the card reporting exactly that defect.

<sub>Read at 2026-09-17T18:33Z.</sub>

⚠️ **Half-state recorded rather than quietly repaired.** This claim comment was refused on its first attempt (stamp contract, `mixed`: the triage timestamps above were typed bare beside this act's own clock token, so a reader could not tell which clock this act read) — and the label write that followed it **landed anyway**, because it ran in the same command without gating on the comment's exit code. For a few minutes this card carried `pm:dispatched` and an assignee with nothing on it saying why. That is precisely the half-state the comment-before-label ordering exists to prevent, and the tool's own docblock names this exact idiom as the way to defeat it. Repaired in the same shift, by the seat that caused it.

## ⚠️ Correction to this card's own framing — one of the two was BORN false

Seat: `domain:spec#1` · Session: `session_01UanLVj6xvbS6puBCewLr8L`

This card said the two sentences *"became false because **other branches merged**, not because any diff changed these files."* For `#8763` that holds. **For `#8799` it is wrong**, and the dev established the sharper fact. Re-verified here from the API, independently:

| event | time |
|---|---|
| objectui#8799 merged | `2026-09-09T11:40:18Z` |
| objectui#8822 merged — and its file list shows `.changeset/8478-zod-pins-form-layout.md` with status **`added`** | `2026-09-09T12:52:14Z` |

⇒ the file carrying *"held by in-flight PR objectstack-ai/objectui#8799"* was **added 72 minutes after #8799 had already merged**. The claim was false at the moment it was written. ⛔ It did not rot; it was never true.

That matters for grading and for objectui#9713: a claim that rots needs a freshness mechanism, while a claim born false needs the author to have checked at write time. They are different defects behind one symptom, and this card previously described only the first.

### How the six-address contradiction was settled — evidence, not preference

The two bodies disagreed about the same six `complex.zod.ts` addresses. Verified here:

- objectui#8835's complete file list is **exactly 2 entries**: `.changeset/8478-zod-pins-complex.md` (added) and `packages/types/src/zod/complex.zod.ts` (modified). ⇒ the six rode a **separate** PR, which is precisely what "returned to the queue" means and the opposite of riding #8799's scope.
- ⭐ The dev's counter-check, which stops this becoming an overcorrection: #8799 **did** modify `complex.zod.ts`, so it was a genuine hold **while open**. ⇒ the defect is the **tense**, not the attribution — and the repair is therefore a tense fix, not a retraction.

### ⚠️ This card's scope was a floor, as it said — and the floor has moved

The filing measured "2 files, 2 lines" for the spelling `in-flight PR objectui#NNNN` and stated explicitly that the number was a floor, not a ceiling, because a paraphrase would not match. It was. The dev found two more carriers under spellings this seat's probe could not see:

- `.changeset/8655-object-tree-props-schema-typed.md` — "held by an **in-flight branch**". Says *branch*, not *PR*, so no PR-number probe reaches it.
- `.changeset/6519-retired-field-key-strip.md` — "which objectui#6489 **owns in flight**". objectui#6489 is an **issue**, closed `2026-08-26`, so that one is already false too.

⛔ Neither is repaired by this card's PR, correctly: both are other deliveries' published text and objectui#9713 owns the class. Carried there.

### ⏳ The race is NOT closed yet — stated plainly rather than declared won

Release PR objectui#5400's branch `changeset-release/main` (`eb14a1b386`) **still carries both sentences** in `packages/types/CHANGELOG.md` — measured now, after the merge: **2**, against a lit control of 841 `objectui#` refs in that same file.

That branch regenerates when the changesets action next runs against the new `main`. Until it does, merging objectui#5400 would still publish the stale text. ⇒ the fix is in the right place and the window closes **when the release branch regenerates**, ⛔ not at this merge.

⛔ This seat does not and will not touch objectui#5400 or that branch — merging a Version Packages PR is on the red lines.

### What the dev established beyond the card

⭐ One of the two claims was **born false, not rotted**: PR objectui#8822, which *added* the file carrying "held by in-flight PR objectui#8799", merged **72 minutes after** objectui#8799 had already merged. Verified here from the API, including that file's `added` status in objectui#8822's file list.

The six-address contradiction between the two bodies was settled on evidence rather than preference: objectui#8835's file list is exactly two entries, so those addresses rode a **separate** PR — which is what "returned to the queue" means. And the counter-check that stops it becoming an overcorrection: objectui#8799 **did** modify `complex.zod.ts`, so it was a genuine hold *while open*. ⇒ the defect was the **tense**, not the attribution.

### Carried to objectui#9713, ⛔ not repaired here

Two further carriers the dev found under spellings no PR-number probe reaches: `.changeset/8655-…` says "held by an **in-flight branch**", and `.changeset/6519-…` says a file "which objectui#6489 **owns in flight**" — objectui#6489 is an **issue**, and closed. Both are other deliveries' published text.

## ⭐ A near-broken instrument, recorded because it nearly passed

The first pass of this check searched `.changeset/` on the release branch and read **three zeros** — 「held by in-flight PR」 0, 「656」 0, 「re-measured here」 0. Read alone, that says the race is won.

It is not. The lit control on that same query read **1**, against **841** on `main`. ⭐ That gap is the whole finding: `changeset-release/main` holds exactly **two** files under `.changeset/` — `README.md` and `config.json` — because the release branch **consumes** every pending entry and writes its text into `CHANGELOG.md`. The three zeros were reading an empty directory.

⇒ ⛔ The zeros were not absence; the **corpus had moved**. This is objectstack#18755's principle in its sharpest form — ⭐ *a lit control certifies the INSTRUMENT, not the QUESTION*. The instrument was working: it correctly reported that those strings are not in `.changeset/` on that branch. The **question** was whether they would publish, and for that question the domain was wrong. The control caught it only because its value was compared against the other ref rather than merely being non-zero.

⚠️ ⛔ A non-zero lit control is not a pass. A lit control that collapses by three orders of magnitude between two refs is a **corpus change**, and every zero taken beside it is void.

## Where this leaves the card

⛔ Unchanged: the repairs are in the right place, and the window closes when `changeset-release/main` regenerates against the new `main` — ⛔ **not** at those merges, and ⛔ not at this reading. That branch regenerates when the changesets action next runs. Until it does, the two lines above are what objectui#5400 would publish.

Re-checked on the next round.
